diagnostics.message:
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook is invoked by the (external) API Gateway and can receive traffic as soon as it exists, but its CloudWatch log group :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.webhook is only created afterwards (the graph currently only has the inverse dependency via the log group's `name = "/aws/lambda/${aws_lambda_function.webhook.function_name}"` reference). If the function is invoked in that window, Lambda auto-creates the log group with default settings (no retention, no KMS), losing the configured retention_in_days/kms_key_id/log_group_class and failing the apply with ResourceAlreadyExistsException. The log group must exist before the function: compute the log group name from var.config.prefix instead of function_name, and add a dependency from the function to the log group (e.g. logging_config.log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.webhook.name, or a bare depends_on once the name reference is removed to avoid a cycle).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_lambda_function.webhook should be created after aws_cloudwatch_log_group.webhook: the log group defines retention/KMS/class settings for the function's /aws/lambda/${function_name} group, and if Lambda is invoked before it exists, Lambda auto-creates the default log group, defeating those settings and causing ResourceAlreadyExists errors on later applies. Note the dependency currently points the wrong way (the log group's name references the function's function_name, and a plain depends_on would form a cycle) — the log group name should be decoupled (e.g. "/aws/lambda/${var.config.prefix}-webhook", matching the function name) so the function can wait on the log group.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_lambda_function.webhook is created before aws_cloudwatch_log_group.webhook (the log group's name references the function, inverting the required order). If the function is invoked before the log group resource is created, Lambda auto-creates a default log group and the aws_cloudwatch_log_group creation then fails with ResourceAlreadyExistsException. The log group must exist before the function can be invoked; note that a bare depends_on would cycle with the current name reference, so the log group name should be derived from var.config.prefix (e.g. "/aws/lambda/${var.config.prefix}-webhook") and the lambda given an explicit depends_on on the log group.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_lambda_function.dispatcher is wired to EventBridge (rule/target) and starts receiving workflow_job events as soon as they are published, but its CloudWatch log group :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.dispatcher is only created after the function (via the `name = "/aws/lambda/${aws_lambda_function.dispatcher.function_name}"` reference). An invocation before the log group exists makes Lambda auto-create it with default settings, losing the configured retention_in_days/kms_key_id/log_group_class and failing the apply with ResourceAlreadyExistsException. The log group must exist before the function: compute the log group name from var.config.prefix instead of function_name, and add a dependency from the function to the log group (e.g. logging_config.log_group = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.dispatcher.name, or a bare depends_on once the name reference is removed to avoid a cycle).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_lambda_function.dispatcher should be created after aws_cloudwatch_log_group.dispatcher: the log group defines retention/KMS/class settings for the function's /aws/lambda/${function_name} group, and if Lambda is invoked before it exists, Lambda auto-creates the default log group, defeating those settings and causing ResourceAlreadyExists errors on later applies. Note the dependency currently points the wrong way (the log group's name references the function's function_name, and a plain depends_on would form a cycle) — the log group name should be decoupled (e.g. "/aws/lambda/${var.config.prefix}-dispatch-to-runner", matching the function name) so the function can wait on the log group.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
aws_lambda_function.dispatcher is created before aws_cloudwatch_log_group.dispatcher (the log group's name references the function, inverting the required order). If the function is invoked (e.g. by the EventBridge target) before the log group resource is created, Lambda auto-creates a default log group and the aws_cloudwatch_log_group creation then fails with ResourceAlreadyExistsException. The log group must exist before the function can be invoked; note that a bare depends_on would cycle with the current name reference, so the log group name should be derived from var.config.prefix (e.g. "/aws/lambda/${var.config.prefix}-dispatch-to-runner") and the lambda given an explicit depends_on on the log group.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook is deployed with vpc_config (when var.config.lambda_subnet_ids/lambda_security_group_ids are set), but it has no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role, which grants the execution role the EC2 network-interface permissions (CreateNetworkInterface, etc.) required for VPC-attached functions. Both resources only depend on aws_iam_role.webhook_lambda/var.config, so the attachment can land after the function is created, causing intermittent CreateFunction failures ("The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface") or failed first invocations. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role]` on the function (no attribute-level data reference exists for a policy attachment, so a bare depends_on is appropriate here; no cycle is introduced).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_lambda_function.webhook should wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role. When var.config.lambda_subnet_ids/lambda_security_group_ids are set, the function is created with vpc_config, and Lambda creates/attaches ENIs on the function's behalf using the execution role — which only has EC2 network-interface permissions once AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole is attached and propagated. The function and attachment share no data reference, so they can be created in parallel.

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
:resource.aws_lambda_function.dispatcher is deployed with vpc_config (when var.config.lambda_subnet_ids/lambda_security_group_ids are set), but it has no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.dispatcher_vpc_execution_role, which grants the execution role the EC2 network-interface permissions (CreateNetworkInterface, etc.) required for VPC-attached functions. Both resources only depend on aws_iam_role.dispatcher_lambda/var.config, so the attachment can land after the function is created, causing intermittent CreateFunction failures ("The provided execution role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface") or failed first invocations. Add `depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.dispatcher_vpc_execution_role]` on the function (no attribute-level data reference exists for a policy attachment, so a bare depends_on is appropriate here; no cycle is introduced).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
aws_lambda_function.dispatcher should wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.dispatcher_vpc_execution_role. When var.config.lambda_subnet_ids/lambda_security_group_ids are set, the function is created with vpc_config, and Lambda creates/attaches ENIs on the function's behalf using the execution role — which only has EC2 network-interface permissions once AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole is attached and propagated. The function and attachment share no data reference, so they can be created in parallel.
